analysis.investment_thesis: A two-year-old condom maker trading at 74x earnings with no track record, no moat, and a market cap of ₹1,274 Cr riding on IPO euphoria. This is precisely the sort of speculative froth a value investor avoids — pay a fortune for a promise, receive a commodity.
key_strengths: Reported ROE of 41.7% suggests current capital efficiency is high
Promoter holding of 62.4% indicates skin in the game
Personal care/FMCG category is understandable and consumable
key_risks: P/E of 73.9 offers zero margin of safety for a startup
Incorporated March 2024 — no operating history across a cycle
ROCE (16.67%) far below ROE (41.7%) suggests leverage-juiced returns
red_flags: Founded barely 2 years ago — IPO hype valuation
Competes against entrenched giants (Manforce, Durex, KamaSutra) with no visible moat
Wide ROE-ROCE gap hints at financial leverage or related-party dynamics
analysis.detailed_analysis:
At 74x earnings for a company barely 24 months old, this is speculation, not investing. The Indian condom market is dominated by well-funded incumbents (Mankind's Manforce, Reckitt's Durex, Raymond's KamaSutra) with decades of brand equity, distribution muscle and shelf-space lock-in. A flavored condom brand called COBRA has no demonstrable moat — no switching costs, no network effects, no cost advantage, and brand power in this category takes decades and hundreds of crores of ad spend to build. The 41.7% ROE looks flattering, but the 25-point gap to ROCE (16.67%) tells me leverage is doing the heavy lifting, which in a capital-light FMCG business is a yellow flag.

I would need to see 7-10 years of earnings, stable operating margins, genuine pricing power, and a price closer to 20x earnings before this fits my circle. An ₹1,274 Cr market cap on a business with no history, at this multiple, requires heroic growth assumptions to merely break even on the investment. Rule No. 1: don't lose money. Rule No. 2: don't forget Rule No. 1. Pass.
